comment: The one source of truth for everything the assistant panel and the embedded Runtime
must agree on. The server validates against this file, the panel imports it, and
tests/test_panel_contract.py refuses any value that only one side knows about.
A constant that lives in two places drifts; F8b is what that costs.
What the timeline says for a state the product publishes without prose of its own.
It used to travel in the event payload as `The agent is working on the request.` --
an English sentence, in a panel whose every other string is Chinese, saying only
that the thing you just started had started.

comment: What a confirmation card asks. A write authorises one exact change and can be
declined. A navigation has one affirmative action; a pre-existing draft can replace
the waiting turn, while an empty composer remains locked.
The standing entry: what the page shows where the assistant will be, before a panel
exists -- while the first connection is still being made, and whenever starting
failed. A person who can only reach a feature through one entry must always find
that entry (P7.5 CR-43). A sentence is a cause, then what happens next; the HTTP
status stays at the end for whoever has to report it. `final_statuses` are the
failures another attempt cannot fix, so none is made on its own.
